items.topic: How to verify the gpt-image-2 API surface (endpoint, params, model ID) before live calls
items.context: Round 1 i5 flagged that the initiative names gpt-image-2, quality tiers, and input_fidelity='high' but cites no endpoint URL, no parameter casing, and no response shape. Finding 4 makes this a research blocker — we cannot run the d1=A test prompts until we know what to call. The verification source also affects how trustworthy the resulting prompt-template sketch is in the conclusion.

options.label: Read current OpenAI Images API docs + the cookbook UI-mockup notebook, record exact endpoint/params/model-ID in the conclusion, then live-smoke-test with one cheapest call
options.rationale: Authoritative source + a single cheap connectivity probe. Catches both stale docs and key-plumbing surprises before we burn budget. Adds maybe 20 minutes.

options.label: Skip docs and infer the schema from a live curl against the endpoint (read errors to discover required params)
options.rationale: Faster but noisier — we'd be doing API archaeology when docs exist. Risks miscoding the cost model if we misread a parameter.

options.label: Defer schema verification — record gpt-image-2/quality/input_fidelity as the names to test against, and leave concrete endpoint pinning to the downstream openai-api-key-plumbing item
options.rationale: Cheapest in research time, but Findings 1-3 (cost model, OpenRouter comparison, style-consistency judgement) all assume the API works as named. If it doesn't, the entire research has to re-run.

items.topic: How to score whether a generated mockup passes the 'would change the user's answer' gate
items.context: Finding 6 elevates the orchestration summary's generation-gate language to the implicit acceptance criterion. The conclusion's go/no-go hinges on whether the test mockups would actually shift a decision answer — but we have no scoring protocol yet. Whichever protocol we pick directly determines what 'go' means for the downstream execute items.

options.label: Self-score: for each test prompt, the researcher (you, here) writes down their pre-image-pick first, then renders the mockup, then notes whether seeing the mockup would have changed the pick. Record the count. Pass = changed-or-confirmed-with-new-info on >=60% of prompts.
options.rationale: Realistic for a 3-5 prompt sample. Honest about the rater being a sample of one. The 60% bar matches 'most decisions benefit, some don't' which is the steady-state we'd ship into.

options.label: User-in-the-loop: deliver the mockups to the actual user (matt) for each test prompt and record their answer-change rate as the score
options.rationale: Highest-quality signal — matches the literal acceptance criterion. Costs the user real time per prompt and adds a synchronous handoff inside the research.

options.label: Skip explicit scoring — record qualitative observations only ('this one looked plausibly useful, this one was decoration') and let the conclusion's go/no-go be a judgement call
options.rationale: Fastest and matches how the spec is currently worded. Loses the ability to defend the recommendation with a concrete number when foundation acts on it.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own scoring protocol or pass bar.

items.topic: How the research harness should persist generated images (also serves as a prototype answer for foundation's open storage question)
items.context: Finding 7: the initiative's orchestration summary lists image storage as an open foundation-level question (local FS vs MinIO vs embedded data URIs in round JSON). Whatever the research harness does will become a de-facto prototype. Picking deliberately means foundation can either adopt or reject it with a clear precedent; picking by accident means re-litigation later.

options.label: Local filesystem under the research item's archive/ folder (one PNG per (prompt, vendor, quality) combination) plus a small index.json mapping
options.rationale: Cheapest, inspectable, ports cleanly into a filesystem-backed production answer. Doesn't pre-commit foundation to a server-side blob store. Keeps the artifacts attached to the research item where reviewers will look for them.

options.label: Embedded base64 data URIs inside round-NNN.json items so the mockups travel with the workshop record
options.rationale: Self-contained — anyone reading the round file sees the images. Bloats round JSONs significantly (medium PNGs ~30-100KB each, base64-encoded inflates ~33%) and stresses Swarm Manager's storage assumptions; not a great precedent for foundation.

options.label: External blob store (MinIO or similar) with URLs in the conclusion
options.rationale: Closest to a likely production answer for the real skill. Massively over-scoped for a research probe — we'd be standing up infra to validate a vendor.

items.topic: API spend budget cap for this research item
items.context: Locked methodology (d1-d4 from round 1) implies roughly: 3-5 prompts × medium tier (~$0.04 each) × 1 with reference image + 1 high-quality comparison + 1-2 OpenRouter spot-checks. Back-of-envelope ~$0.50-$2.00 plus retries. A budget cap is normally implicit, but for autonomously executed research a number lets the harness self-stop instead of running until something breaks.

options.label: Hard cap of $5 in cumulative API spend across OpenAI + OpenRouter; abort and report partial results if exceeded
options.rationale: ~3-5x expected spend gives headroom for retries, OpenRouter price surprises, and a couple of high-quality renders without going off the rails.

options.label: Hard cap of $20 — generous enough that a full-matrix comparison would still fit if we changed our minds mid-research
options.rationale: More flexibility, but risks silently optimising the research toward 'use up the budget' rather than 'answer the question cheaply'.

options.label: No explicit cap — measure and report actual spend in the conclusion
options.rationale: Simplest. Acceptable since the working assumption is sub-$5 anyway. Gives no protection against a parameter mistake that re-renders everything at the high tier.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own cap or budgeting rule.

items.text: Round 1 outcome incorporated: all four decisions accepted as A. Methodology section of conclusion.md is now locked to historical-prompts (d1=A), medium-quality default (d2=A), 1-2 prompt OpenRouter spot-check (d3=A), and a single Vrooli screenshot as style anchor (d4=A). Subsequent rounds will not re-litigate these unless new findings invalidate them.

Prompt-template rules already exist upstream: orchestration-summary.md for ai-image-generation-foundation records the cookbook-derived rules (present-tense 'as if shipped', no concept-art vocabulary, layout → hierarchy → spacing → real interface elements → constraints, device framing, reference-image carries style). The research's prompt-template sketch should treat these as given and only add findings that emerge from the test runs — avoiding the trap of re-deriving the cookbook in this conclusion.

Storage question is foundation-level, not just research-internal: the orchestration summary explicitly calls out image-storage location as an open question to be 'resolved by the research item + handoff-propagation item together.' d3 elevates this from an implementation detail of the test harness to a deliberate prototype contribution back to the initiative.

Unverified-API risk is a single-point-of-failure for the whole research: if the gpt-image-2 model ID, the input_fidelity parameter name, or the quality tier names have moved since the initiative doc was written, every downstream finding (cost, comparison, style consistency) becomes wrong without the conclusion noticing. d1 puts a verification step in front of the live calls so we fail fast instead of fail-quietly.

No Vrooli UI screenshots were found in the agent-manager repo at /home/matthalloran8/.local/share/workspace-sandbox/.../merged (no PNG/JPG assets, no screenshots/ or assets/ directories). The d4=A reference image will need to be sourced from the actual Vrooli scenario repo or captured at research-execution time. Worth flagging now so the harness builder doesn't assume the asset is checked in here.
